body: As this is edition 2018, you can instead use `log::info!("Hello")` (or import `use log::info`) everywhere and not worry about `#[macro_use]` here. Personally I find I like seeing `log::error!("danger")` instead of `error!("danger")` anyway.
Likewise you can delete all these extern crate declarations.

This operation is actually implemented in bitflags for you. Just `repo_file_statuses.iter().collect()`. The `.collect()` iterator adapter is controlled through `FromIterator` trait (which bitflags implements for all of the flag types it generates).

This is currently converting `git2::Statuses` to a single `git2::Status`. It doesn't seem I'm able to output a `git2::Status` with `repo_file_statuses.iter().collect()`. 🤔 

```
a collection of type `git2::Status` cannot be built from an iterator over elements of type `git2::StatusEntry<'_>`
```

Hm. I see. I feel `Statuses::status` method should probably exist but I'm not the `git2` guys.

---

You can adapt my snippet like this for it to work:

```rust
let repo_status: Status = repo_file_statuses.iter().map(|e| e.status()).collect();
```

You're not saving much on code complexity but its declarative so I think its still a small improvement.
I think it could be a good idea to add a little table to the `README` to help act as an easy reference for understanding these little guys 👍
This is cool will make debugging a lot easier 👍 Just want to double check if its still in there on purpose :)
`as_ref` is neat, didn't know you could do that 👍

Yep, it's in there on purpose. 😄
I'd like to eventually go back and add detailed trace and debug logs to make it clear what the prompt is doing under the hood.
